finding: A nested repository inside a worktree under <root>/<short name> is mapped to the outer listed entry instead of being treated as not listed.
why: With root /r and listed /m (short name m), an agent in /r/m/wt1/vendor/lib (its own clone) gets _git_top = .../vendor/lib, find_entry matches it by the <root>/m text, and the entry for /m is returned without asking git, so check_target('/away/lib-wt') is refused as outside /r/m though lib is not listed; the same layout inside the main checkout answers not listed.
fix: Accept an entry matched only through the root when top is a worktree (.git is a file and no repository sits between <root>/<short name> and top); otherwise fall through to git; add tests for a nested clone and a submodule inside a worktree.
evidence:
if entry is not None and (_key(entry.path) == _key(top) or not _below(top, entry.path)):
            return entry

criterion: Checking a chosen target: links resolved on both sides
finding: check_target collapses `..` by text before links are resolved, so `<root>/<short>/<link>/../x` can read as inside while its real target is elsewhere.
why: os.path.normpath here, and os.path.abspath inside repo_list.normalize used by _below, fold link/.. textually before realpath runs, so 'links resolved' holds only for links not followed by '..'.
fix: Resolve the joined, un-normalized target with os.path.realpath before comparing, and add a test with <link>/../x where the link points outside the folder.
evidence: return _place(folder, environ, os.path.normpath(absolute), None); Acceptance: 'links and drive-letter case are resolved on both sides'

finding: target_for and check_target on an unlisted repository can still raise PlacementError, because root_state() parses the machine file before the listed check.
why: The settled design says placement answers 'not listed' before it can fail (design.round.json:648; INV-014; AC-055), but a malformed machine file raises here even for an unlisted repository, so the guard would fail every agent command in any repository.
fix: When the root cannot be read, look up the entry without the root; answer not listed when none is found and raise only for a listed repository; add a test.

finding: Possible information leakage: R-06 re-implements the short-name folder ownership rule that repo_list owns, through its private helpers.
why: repo_list._claim (scripts/repo_list.py:342-352) decides 'folder absent/empty, or marker names this repo' and placement copies the same decision while calling repo_list._marker_holder, _check_short_name and MARKER_NAME, so a change to the marker protocol edits both modules in lockstep.
fix: Export one public read-only folder-ownership check from repo_list used by both _claim and placement, and make placement call only public repo_list names.
evidence: held = repo_list._marker_holder(pathlib.Path(folder) / repo_list.MARKER_NAME)  [also line 147: repo_list._check_short_name(name)]

criterion: Happy-path-only (no off-boundary values around new comparisons)
finding: No test puts a target at a sibling whose name shares the short-name prefix (<root>/proj-x/y against <root>/proj).
why: _below is a string-prefix comparison (startswith(parent + os.sep)); no outside case tests the prefix edge, so dropping the separator would pass every test.
fix: Add an outside case root / 'proj-extra' / 'x' to the parametrized outside test.
evidence: "another short name": root / "other" / "x"  vs  _below: child_key.startswith(parent_key.rstrip("\\/") + os.sep)

criterion: Happy-path-only (negative cases for a recorded decision)
finding: D-35 (a repository git cannot map to a main checkout counts as not listed) has no test.
why: _main_by_git returns None when the common dir is not `.git` and has no core.worktree; only the submodule path and the GIT_DIR path are exercised, so a change to refuse here would pass.
fix: Add a test with a worktree of a repository made with --separate-git-dir, asserting not listed.
evidence: DECISIONS.md D-35: "Chosen: B — answer not listed"; _main_by_git: `if done.returncode != 0 or not done.stdout.strip(): return None`

finding: Possible transposition trap: check_target takes (target, folder) while target_for takes (folder, name).

fix: Make folder keyword-only in check_target before 0005/0006 consume it.

finding: Result types are undocumented: which fields each state sets, and that 'outside' is a rule value, not a state.
why: Consumers branch on bare-string state and rule; the per-state shape is predictable from the code but stated nowhere (verify pass: downgraded from medium).
fix: Add a short note on the result types naming the fields each state sets.
evidence:
class Verdict(NamedTuple):
    state: str
    target: str | None
    folder: str | None = None
    rule: str | None = None

finding: Possible stale-module reuse: _load returns whatever already sits in sys.modules['afk_config'].
why: If a process loaded afk_config from a different file first, placement uses it silently and parse_single_file may be missing (AttributeError instead of PlacementError).
fix: Reuse a loaded module only when it was loaded from the same file; otherwise load under a placement-private name.
evidence: afk_config = _load("afk_config", "afk-config.py")

finding: The read-budget test pins an exact open count of 4 on top of the allowed-set check.
why: Caching or merging the list read is behaviour-preserving and would break the test, while the acceptance only says no other file is opened.

evidence:

    assert len(opened) == 4, opened

finding: R-06 branches for an unreadable marker and for a short-name path that is a file have no test.
why: _short_name_folder has distinct outcomes ('is not a folder', 'reserved for an unreadable marker') that no test reaches.

finding: Several test bodies branch or loop to steer setup or asserts.
why: A failure in the loop test does not say which layout broke, and the R-01 assert loosens to an `or` of two messages.
fix: Parameterize on the raw machine-file text and on the layouts instead of branching in the body; assert the reason per case.

finding: Possible information leakage: git's main-checkout derivation is known by both placement and repo_list.
why: repo_list.main_checkout/_separate_git_main already own 'which main checkout does git name for a folder', and _main_by_git re-derives it.
fix: Give repo_list a main-checkout lookup that accepts the caller's environment and use it from placement.
evidence: done = _git(folder, environ, "config", "--file", os.path.join(common, "config"), "--get", "core.worktree")

finding: Possible leakage of rule semantics: orchestration compares against the literal id R-01 and picks rules by a scope string.
why: _place knows only an R-01 failure leaves root.path unusable and filters ROOT_RULES by strings at two sites, so a reordered or added catalog row breaks the chain silently.
fix: Carry the 'path unusable' fact on RootState and expose the root and short-name chains as two named tuples.
evidence: rooted = root.rule != "R-01"
